Specification: abs — Absolute Value of an Integer

1. Overview

  abs is a total function over the integers. It maps any integer x to a
  non-negative integer representing its distance from zero on the number line.

2. Signature

  abs : Z -> Z

3. Definition

  For all integers x:

      abs(x) =  x    if x >= 0
      abs(x) = -x    if x <  0

4. Expected Properties

  For all integers x:

      P1. Non-negativity:  abs(x) >= 0
      P2. Identity case:   abs(x) = x    if x >= 0
      P3. Negation case:   abs(x) = -x   otherwise (i.e., if x < 0)

5. Corollaries

  C1. abs(0) = 0
  C2. abs(x) = abs(-x)              (symmetry)
  C3. x <= abs(x)                   (abs dominates its argument)
  C4. abs(x) = 0  <=>  x = 0        (zero only for zero)
